title: MEPS event payment bands do not form a monotonic later-health or bill gradient
source_unit: MEPS 2024 person records with first ER or inpatient event strictly between R3/1 and R4/2, conditioned on event-level family-paid amount

observations.period: 2024; first emergency-room event in strict inter-round window, by family-paid amount band

denominator.unit: event-window people; outcome-specific valid denominators vary

zero_payment_baseline_fair_or_poor_healt.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 1.85 pp

zero_payment_followup_fair_or_poor_healt.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 1.99 pp

zero_payment_followup_bill_problem.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 1.80 pp

positive_under_100_followup_bill_problem.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 3.65 pp

100_or_more_followup_bill_problem.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 2.89 pp

observations.method: First event month strictly after R3/1 and strictly before R4/2 endpoint month; payment band is zero, positive under $100, or $100 and above using event-level family-paid amount; outcomes use PERWT24F and 128 BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: Family-paid amount is not a complete bill, balance, or household burden. Payment bands inherit event severity, payer, coverage, and selection differences; the small positive-under-$100 cell is imprecise.
observations.subgroup: First emergency-room event in the strict inter-round window.
observations.counterinterpretation: Zero payment may reflect public or private coverage, imputation, payer mix, or an event with no recorded family payment rather than low burden; higher payment may mark severity rather than unaffordability.

observations.period: 2024; first inpatient event in strict inter-round window, by family-paid amount band

denominator.unit: event-window people; outcome-specific valid denominators vary

zero_payment_baseline_fair_or_poor_healt.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 3.15 pp

zero_payment_followup_fair_or_poor_healt.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 3.46 pp

zero_payment_followup_bill_problem.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 2.34 pp

positive_under_100_followup_bill_problem.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 5.32 pp

100_or_more_followup_bill_problem.unit: percent; weighted share; BRR SE 2.47 pp

observations.method: First event month strictly after R3/1 and strictly before R4/2 endpoint month; payment band is zero, positive under $100, or $100 and above using event-level family-paid amount; outcomes use PERWT24F and 128 BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: Payment is event-level family contribution, not a full obligation; the positive-under-$100 inpatient cell has 34 people and wide intervals. Baseline selection and event severity remain.
observations.subgroup: First inpatient event in the strict inter-round window.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower bill-problem share at higher payment can reflect coverage, payer mix, severity, payment capacity, or reporting rather than lower burden.

related_sources.claim: The strict event window preserves baseline selection before follow-up.
The first-event ledger defines payment as event-level family/self payment and preserves its household-burden boundary.

boundary: This is a payment-band conditioned descriptive transition. It does not identify a complete bill, payment obligation, care choice, alternative, household adaptation, remedy, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
